utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: After this hour, hour-and-a-half meeting that you've described for us where Mr. Beara was present, can you tell us if you had ever met him at any time subsequent to that?

utterances.speaker: JAKOV BIENENFELD
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And sir, just so we have it on the record and to be clear, are you familiar or are you friends with any members of his family?

utterances.speaker: JAKOV BIENENFELD
utterances.text: I remember that somebody once told me that he has two children, but I don't know them. I don't know how old they are, what they look like. He could be about ten years older than I am, so I can assume the age of the children, but I don't have any idea, and I never saw them, and I didn't even see Mr. Beara after that. Now is the first time that I'm seeing him.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And sir, can you just tell me again, you mentioned Zarko Keza Can you tell me what his role was in this evacuation of the people from Sarajevo who participated in this meeting that you recall?

utterances.speaker: JAKOV BIENENFELD
utterances.text: Zarko Keza -- well, he was assigned to me from the SIS, which is the equivalent of the KOS, to help me, and he was some sort of assistant of something.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: During this meeting, were you able to observe whether or not Mr. Beara had any prejudices or bias towards any ethnic group?

utterances.speaker: JAKOV BIENENFELD
utterances.text: Look, sir, I'm not dealing with the attitudes or the positions of Mr. Beara. He was a very good professional at that time, so I didn't do that. I did not enter into the reasons why the treatment of the Jewish community within the Republika Srpska and within the Republic of Croatia and within Bosnia was more than satisfactory. I didn't notice any bias. If I had noticed any, I would have stood up and ended the conversation.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Based upon your observations, sir, who in your view was the most instrumental in making sure that there was this safe passage through Republika Srpska for these convoys that you were assisting to evacuate?

utterances.speaker: JAKOV BIENENFELD
utterances.text: I personally think that Mr. Ljubisa Beara was a person in whose technical jurisdiction was security, so in a way we were part of his duty. And also, I sincerely and deeply believe that he was up to his neck involved in any convoy that was leaving Republika Srpska near Stolac. I cannot believe that he was not involved in some way.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And just a couple more questions, and thank you for your patience. You told us that there were seven convoys that you among others, obviously, during your position as head of security for the Zagreb Jewish community. But can you give us a better estimate to the best of your recollection as to approximately how many people of multiethnic identities were on these convoys that were being evacuated from Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: JAKOV BIENENFELD
utterances.text: My estimate -- I mean, we didn't have the precise record. Probably we could find the exact information at the Jewish community office in Zagreb. According to my records, it's about 16 or 1700 people of which were legitimate and registered members of the Jewish communities of Sarajevo, 500, and the rest were just people from throughout the area. So it was perhaps 1200, 1300, 1400 people.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. I have no further questions at this time. Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Does any team of other Defence has cross-examination? I see none. Mr. Elderkin.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: In fact, I'd just like to thank you Mr. Bienenfeld for coming, and we also have no questions for him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Ostojic?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I apologise for interrupting. I'm told that on line 59 -- on page 59, line 13, actually the reference was to Stolac, S-T-O-L-A-C, without the K, but just so we have that, but we'll look into it, but I think that's the way it should be spelled.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: What is the line again? 13?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I have it. I didn't highlight it accurately, but I thought -- actually, we could ask the witness to clarify that maybe.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: No, I was asking what the reference of the transcript page and line.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Page 59, line 13.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: It's part of your question? Probably my line is different from yours.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Well, I found it now, and I have it. I think we're looking at the same thing. It's line 17, which is part of the answer, and I apologise for that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Oh, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Do you see it now?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I apologise, and thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Bienenfeld. That concludes your testimony here. On behalf of the Tribunal, I thank you for your coming to give it. Now you are free to go.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Do you have any documents to tender, Mr. Ostojic?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: We do not, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Is the next witness ready?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I believe the next witness is ready, and it's Professor Gogic, and Mr. Nikolic will lead the evidence with him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: You need some short break in order to prepare?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Just to maybe -- no, I don't think so, but if the Court wants.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Let's bring him in, then.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Good morning, Professor. If you could take a solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, please be seated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Nikolic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. I'm just going to wait a little for my learned friend.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Good day, Mr. Gogic.

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR GOGIC
utterances.text: Good day.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Mr. Gogic, are you ready? Can we begin?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR GOGIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I'm going to introduce myself. It's required for the transcript. I'm Predrag Nikolic representing Mr. Beara in his Defence team. I'm going to be questioning you today on behalf of the Defence team. Now, I'm going to ask you to introduce yourself.

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR GOGIC
utterances.text: My name is Ljubomir Gogic. I was born on the 10th of December, 1958, in Sarajevo. I work at the criminal investigations expertise of the criminal investigation centre of the MUP of Republika Srpska in Banja Luka, and I work as an expert on handwriting bills or paper bills and signatures.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Mr. Gogic, can you please tell us your qualifications, your education?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR GOGIC
utterances.text: I completed the faculty of theology the department of psychology and pedagogy in 1971 in Sarajevo. I did not complete, but I did attend the post-doctoral studies. I became -- and I completed half of the requirements for a masters degree, but because of the war I had to interrupt my studies.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: The faculty was completed in 1981 in Sarajevo, not '71.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can you please tell us what duties and what jobs you carried out?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR GOGIC
utterances.text: After completing my studies in psychology and pedagogy, from 1983 to 1986 I worked as the assistant -- teaching assistant at the faculty of philosophy in Zadar, which was part of the Split University. Because of family problems that I have, my parents' illness, I returned to Sarajevo, my home town, and in 1986 I got a job at the Ministry of the Interior of the socialist republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina in the criminal technology department sector of the crime-fighting department on handwriting documents and signature expertise. I then from 1986 until 1992 worked at the MUP of the socialist republic of Bosnia Herzegovina, and because of the war this was suspended when the MUP of Republika Srpska was formed and the department of criminal expertise where I then transferred to the MUP of Republika Srpska in Banja Luka in the unit that exclusively deals with expertise including expertise on documents, handwriting, and signatures. In 1995, I was appointed by the justice ministry as an in-house expert for documents, handwriting, and signature as a graphologist expert, although that is not the best possible description of that job. On the 20 --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter didn't understand the date.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- I was appointed as the permanent court expert for handwriting, documents, signatures by the basic and the appeals Court of the Brcko district of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Gogic, I'm going to ask you to repeat the date when you became the court expert because that was not entered in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR GOGIC
utterances.text: Yes. On the 23rd of August, 1995, I was appointed as the permanent graphologist expert by the justice ministry and the administration of Republika Srpska. It was a certificate of the minister --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter did not catch the number.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- and then on the 26th of July, 2002, I was appointed as permanent graphic expert -- graphology expert for documents, signatures, and handwriting. On the 26th of July, 2002, I was appointed as a court expert in documents, handwriting, and signature expertise by the appeals and basic court of the Brcko district of Bosnia and Herzegovina, 249/02 of the court and also by the decision number 604/02 of the same court.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Gogic, I'm first going to ask you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Gogic, I take it you are reading from your CV. Am I correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm going to ask you to speak more slowly especially when discussing numbers. But I also received the information that on page 62, line 24, it has been entered what you studied. I would like you to repeat that. What it says here is theology, but actually I would like you to complete that.

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR GOGIC
utterances.text: I completed studies of pedagogy and psychology at the faculty of philosophy in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Nikolic, what I meant is that because we have the CV, so you can go through a bit more quickly with respect to his CV.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. I just wanted to ask the witness to speak more slowly, and I was going to go to the heart of the matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Sir, could you please provide us some more details about the work of your department. What are the tasks that you were involved in?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR GOGIC
utterances.text: When it comes to forensic analysis, we establish the originality of documents; we analyse the paper of the document with regard to the property, the size, the colour, the chemical composition, the identification of the means for writing, whether be it a ballpoint pen, felt tip pen, pencil. We also identify typing, typewriters, electronic -- mechanical typewriters, inkjet, laser, thermal, printers, and so on, so forth. We also identified the integrality of typing. We also identify the typing cartridges, the type of printing in terms of -- there's being offset, high, or deep. We'd identify photocopied and scanned documents. We identify the systems of writing. We also identify scriptors, the handwritings -- the handwriting of figures and signatures. We also identify scriptors with regard to the chronological age, the physical and mental status of the writer. We also identify the influence of the instruments and the position in writing on the handwriting.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please slow down.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Professor Gogic, if you could slow down for the benefit of the interpreters in your answer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I think you need to repeat the last part of your answer, but if Mr. Nikolic could attend to it.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Mr. Gogic, could you just briefly explain to the Trial Chamber, what are the tasks are involved in graphological analysis that you have performed as a member of the -- your department in the Ministry of the Interior?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR GOGIC
utterances.text: The collation of the originality of documents to see whether the document was forged. Moreover, identification of the device that was used, be it a mechanical, electrical, electromechanical, electronic, writers, printers, thermal, dot matrix.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: I apologise, Mr. Gogic. I have to interrupt you before you start repeating yourself. In your explanation, you arrived at an explanation with regard to the establishment of the method of handwriting and so and so forth. I would like you to tell us more because this is relevant, I don't want you to go over the same grounds again, I'm going to remind you, you left it off with the establishment or detection of the synchronous on asynchronous types of handwriting. Can you tell us something about that when it comes to the establishment of these?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR GOGIC
utterances.text: When it comes to the establishment of the absolute or relevant age of a document, there are three methods available to us. The first one is to establish the absolute age of the ink; the establishment of the relative age of the document, i.e., the establishment of the fact that if something was created simultaneously or whether something was created before or after; and the third method is the method of detection of the synchronous and asynchronous inscription, i.e., separate or sequential inscription. And in that sense, there are appropriate criteria, i.e., starting points for the procedure to detect separate from sequential inscription. These criteria and starting points are based on the relevant number of different research projects, primarily those that were so-called case studies which were based on the investigation of different handwritings in various journals, logbooks, and other materials where contents are entered, in which especially important is Robert Foley's research. He investigated 500 documents of a known but different origin - originating from government and other organizations - arrived at a general conclusion, and established a set of criteria that might serve as a starting point for the differentiation of one from another.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Mr. Gogic, when we are talking about the research of documents and the establishment of facts that you've just spoken about, did you undergo any other courses or types of education? And if you did, could you tell us something about that?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR GOGIC
utterances.text: After the war, I believe that this was in the year 2000, in the organisation of the American Ministry of Justice, I attended a seminar in Sarajevo which was led by Gideon Epstein, one of the top authorities across the world in this area of forensic analysis. For awhile he was also the president of the American association of experts on the investigation of documents and document analysis, and he's also well known for the fact that he was a member of the team of investigators of the war crimes committed by Joseph Mengele. A person under the pseudonym Helmut Gregor in Sao Paolo was identified by him as Josef Mengele based on the handwritings and the handwritten notes of that person. After that in the month of September 2001, I spent some time at the forensic institute at the headquarters of the German federal police in Weisbaden in -- it's the KT-5 department, which deals primarily in the forensic analysis of handwriting and signatures headed by Mr. Manfred Hecker, who is famous for having created a system of the investigation of handwriting, the so-called FISH system, standing for the Forensic Information System of Handwriting, which was also taken over by the FBI amongst other organizations.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Mr. Gogic, when you attended these seminars, did you receive certain qualifications? Did you receive certificates certifying your attendance and the knowledge that you acquired?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR GOGIC
utterances.text: Yes, we did obtain certificates after these seminars. Those were attendance certificates testifying to the -- to their successful completion.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: At the very beginning of your testimony, you said that you are also a forensic expert in graphology in Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR GOGIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us something about that, primarily what does it entail? What does your forensic expertise entail when you work as a forensic expert?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR GOGIC
utterances.text: When a Court or a Prosecutor's Office issues an order or request or when police organizations issue such requests, I mostly perform the same duties and tasks I perform in the department for forensic analysis at the police. In other words, I examine documents, bank notes, handwritings, and signatures.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Mr. Gogic, tell us a bit more about the methodology that you use in your forensic analysis.

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR GOGIC
utterances.text: When it comes to the forensic analysis of handwriting and signatures, we apply the so-called comparative methodology based on special and general handwriting characteristics; to be more specific, a disputable handwriting and the handwriting of the suspects who might have been the authors of the document. In that sense, in order to be able to embark on any forensic analysis, one has to study in detail the object of the expertise or analysis. In this particular case as it would be a handwritten document, one has to establish the general characteristics of that handwriting and -- as well as very specific individual features of that handwriting as departing elements for the procedure and methodology of comparison with the equally established characteristics of the handwriting of the suspects in question.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Did you also use the same method when you drafted your report on the task given to you by the Defence team?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR GOGIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Mr. Gogic, when was it that you had first contact with the Ljubisa Beara Defence team?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR GOGIC
utterances.text: I believe that this was towards the end of March or the beginning of April of this year.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Were you provided with all the necessary documentation, and if you did, what kind of documentation did you receive, and were you also provided with a detailed instruction as to what you were expected to do?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR GOGIC
utterances.text: Yes. I received documentation, but I received photocopies. I received three photocopied books or logs, the logbook of the duty operations officer that was marked by number 02935619 on the cover page; also, the logbook of the IKM Kitovnice marked by the following number on the cover page, 00760268; and the auxiliary logbook marked by the following number, 02936603.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Nikolic, for clarity could we have the 65 ter numbers of those three logbooks? First, the duty operation logbook.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just going to do that. Just a moment, sir. It would be 2D -- I apologise, 7DP00378.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Your Honours, I think I can assist the Trial Chamber. In order, they would be Exhibits 377, that was the first one that was number 02935619, what we referred to as the duty officer notebook; the second document would be P935, that would be the IKM notebook; and then the final one is Exhibit 378 -- I believe 7DP378.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. I think that's correct, Mr. Nikolic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Absolutely correct, and I thank my learned friend for her assistance.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Mr. Gogic, kindly tell us what was your brief given to you by the Beara Defence team?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR GOGIC
utterances.text: By my specific expertise of the documents, it was necessary to establish the following: whether the pages in question have been altered, whether anything was added, retraced, or whether there were any changes of any kind that would violate their authenticity and integrity. Then we would need to see if any scriptor, one or several, were used to write the handwriting on the pages in question or not, and then to compare - as the third task - the characteristics of the handwriting on the pages to classify them, group the different handwritings according to their common characteristics. Then the fourth assignment would be -- which what was written by Jokic, Trbic, Obrenovic, and Nikolic on these pages, whether there were any words or numbers added on those pages or inserted there and if the handwriting was created asynchronously or separately for themselves or synchronously sequentially in a series. The sixth assignment is if there were any insertions, where they are; and the seventh task would be to differentiate between the different means of scripting.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Of all these tasks, did you complete all of them? Were you able to complete all of them?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR GOGIC
utterances.text: All the tasks were completed except one, and that is the one under number 4 that I referred to in the sense of whether the scriptors of the contents in these diaries, Jokic, Nikolic, Trbic, and Obrenovic, in view of the fact that I didn't have their handwriting as a comparison and also in the diaries. If there is the participation of these scriptors, it was not indicated what specifically they wrote. So for the above reasons, I was not able to approach the procedure of comparative analysis of their handwriting or the characteristics of their handwriting with the characteristics of the handwriting that I found and which structure these referred-to diaries.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: After this assignment, how many reports did you complete?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR GOGIC
utterances.text: There are two reports. The first one was a report which was done and forwarded on the basis of an analysis of documents which were photocopies. In view of the fact that in order to provide a specific opinion, one requires original documents. I asked or sought the possibility to have access and review original documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Did you have an opportunity - and if you did, when and where - to look at the original documents?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR GOGIC
utterances.text: Yes. The original documents I reviewed at the premises of the Prosecutor's Office of The Hague Tribunal in late June of this year, and I did this in order to analyse and review the documents right there.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: After looking at the original documents, did you draft another report based on the original documents?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR GOGIC
utterances.text: Yes. On the basis of the reviewed original documents at the OTP of The Hague Tribunal and the expertise done on the ink, which was conducted at the institute of forensics here in The Hague, a report -- a new report was drafted, and that is the second report that has also been included here.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Just one moment, I'm going to refer to this new report so that we can all follow. That is number 2D582. Mr. Gogic, is this report any different than the other report that was drafted on the basis of photocopies, and if it is, what are the differences?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR GOGIC
utterances.text: The differences are that the ink was analysed, and then on the basis of those results that section was added to the previous report, and also in view of the fact that an expertise was conducted on the originals and not on the photocopies of the documents, the opinion given was more firm, more decisive.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, we have made a small introduction, and now we would like to embark on analysis of the report. If you think that this is now a good moment, we could go on a break and then move to more specific parts of this witness's testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I think it's a convenient time, but before we take a break, I remember -- whether -- I'm not sure that Ms. Soljan can address this. I remember Mr. McCloskey referred to a comparison book or the -- which will contain the both B/C/S and English, and there was an issue whether to include the comment from the Prosecution or not, but what happened to -- can I hear the further development?

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Your Honours, on the 14th of December during a trial session, it was decided that the Prosecution's annotation would not be treated as evidence by the Trial Chamber but that this book could be used as an aid in an approach to it. And this -- I believe in e-court it is set out as 377(A), but obviously we have given hard copies of this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: It has the both B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Which - exactly - has both B/C/S/ and English with annotations on it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I don't remember we have received that in hard copies, but do you have hard copies available?

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Your Honours, we do have them available.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: It would be very beneficial.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Absolutely, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Okay, we will take a break for 25 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Nikolic, please continue your examination. We may need about five minutes at the end of the session for our ruling.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Mr. Gogic, I would like to move to an analysis or an explanation of the report that you furnished. But before that, I would ask you to explain some terms that you referred to before the break, primarily referring to the way things are written. You mentioned sequential and separate writing. Can you please explain these terms for us in the context of your testimony?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR GOGIC
utterances.text: As for the meanings of separate or asynchronous marks, the basic characteristics of this writing is -- are that the previous position of the hand in writing has to be, again, repositioned for the following separate writing, so it indicates a slower more thought-out writing, an upright position of the letters, larger letters and numbers, shorter words, occasional ornamentation, greater or lighter pressure of the ink stroke, increase legibility of the contents, alignment to the margin, and random shaping of the letters. When we're talking about sequential writing or serial writing, once the hand position and the position of the fist is established during the writing, it remains until a certain line of script is completed. They are also characterized by a greater speed of writing and the slant of the letters and the numbers. There is reduced legibility, and the letters are less compact and the pressure is less. The letters are more drawn out or squashed. The regularity of the series of script, consistent use of a certain shape of a letter or a number. There are some others, but these are the most prominent characteristics of the two types of script or writing.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I forgot one important piece of information. Mr. Gogic's report has been translated into English, and we can look at it on page 2D410018. This is the English version, and in the B/C/S version the number is starting from page 2D41-0001. I think that this will be useful.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Now, we can go back to your findings. Mr. Gogic, you said that you looked at all of these books. Did you concentrate on the entire books, or did you just look at specific pages?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR GOGIC
utterances.text: I looked at the entire books, but my attention was exclusively focused on the pages that I was asked to review by Mr. Beara's Defence team.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I would like to ask you to analyse one of the pages for us, and that would be a page from Exhibit P00377, page RN02935741. Mr. Gogic, if you can see -- well, let's wait a little bit. We'll wait until it appears.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Your Honours, just -- we have the originals of the notebooks here in the event that they want -- the Defence wants to use them.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I guess it would be good to hand the originals to Mr. Gogic so then he can show us on the ELMO the elements which are important in his findings.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: I'm going to ask to look at page 02935741. Mr. Gogic, the original page that you have in front of you, can you place it on the ELMO? I'm going to ask the usher to help us, if she can, and I would like to ask you in accordance with the task that you were given by the Defence team to explain what you find on this page in terms of your task and to indicate those places to us. Do you have the page in front of you?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR GOGIC
utterances.text: No. I have it here, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Mr. Gogic?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR GOGIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes. I have the attachment, and I have it on the screen. On the page numbered 02935741, it has been established that there are traces of tracing and alterations. The alterations are --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We have it in e-court so that the witness can mark on the B/C/S version. Can we zoom out so that -- I'll leave it in your hands, Mr. Nikolic. For the record, I take it to be the -- page 123, 123 of that logbook in e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Gogic. I would now like to ask you to show us pursuant to the task you were given on this page what you established and to circle that with a felt tip pen so that we could note that.

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR GOGIC
utterances.text: What was established here are traces of alterations. [Witness marks], also signs of retracing here, another sign of alterations here. It was noted in the ink analysis that the same ink was used in the writing of the original and in the retracing and alterations.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Mr. Gogic, one of the tasks was also to establish if these documents - specifically this one and the following one - were written by one writer or several of them. So my question would be in terms of this page, if this was written by one writer or several of them?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR GOGIC
utterances.text: The entire handwriting of the numbers and the figures is of one scriptor, whom I indicated as scriptor A.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Thank you. The retracing and alterations, are they, and - if yes - to which degree to they affect the authenticity of this document?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR GOGIC
utterances.text: Alterations and retracing were mostly done at items number 2 and number 4 - I think that is here - and lower case and upper case D with the word "dule," and then also retracing at the beginning of the page. When you have such retracing or alterations, their nature is not such that it would have any significant effect on the authenticity of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: I would also like to ask you the following: The types of script here, what sort of handwriting are they?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR GOGIC
utterances.text: This is the sequential script.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: All right. Before we finish with these documents, can you please look at the bottom and place your name and the date at the bottom of this page so that this particular page would be verified?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR GOGIC
utterances.text: [Witness marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: You talked about alterations and retracing. I would like to ask you to mark them in a different way, what was specifically altered in the document, and we can mark that with the letter A, and we can mark the retracings with the letter B, and that way it would be more clear.

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR GOGIC
utterances.text: [Witness marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I would like to now look at Document R02935742. This document and all the others that we will go through in the same way, I would like to tender as evidence. We have the document. Mr. Gogic, I would like to ask you to analyse this document from the aspect of how many scriptors there were, one or several, and to explain if there are other elements that would be the subject of your notice. In the same way, we are going to try to identify everything that you established.

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR GOGIC
utterances.text: The handwriting on page 02935742 was produced by three scriptors. The handwriting from the beginning, beginning with the asterisks and the word "Vukotic" and the contents, "lovac 2", and the arrow was written -- I'm sorry. Actually, it's two scriptors, not three. I made an error. So from the beginning, from -- from the beginning until "lovac 2" was written by one scriptor as well as the contents above the underlined word "aco." Where there is a dash and a content that can be partially identified, it says something, "na dza se," [phoen] something in that sense, and this was written by one scriptor. The second scriptor wrote the contents that begin from the middle of the page beginning with the word that starts with the capital letter T, and ends with the words "Beara." On this page we have examples of retracing, alteration, and crossing-out. Places where there was retracing are here. [Witness marks] Alterations can be seen here, and crossing-out, here. In order to write the content on this page, two colours of ink were used, blue and black, and the actual things written by the first scriptor, scriptor A, was written by a blue pen of a referent composition of that type while the contents written by the second scriptor who I marked as scriptor C until the last word "Beara" was written, the text was written by a black ballpoint pen. On this page there are sequential and separately written contents. Scriptor A wrote sequentially and scriptor C including the last paragraph, but the word "Vukotic" is written separately in front of the word "da," as well as there is an example of separate script with this already-mentioned entry that is above the underlined word "aco", which can be read as, dash, "dzefin dzafin" [phoen]. This is an example of separate script.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Mr. Gogic, can you also show us and encircle the parts written by scriptor A and those written by scriptor C?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR GOGIC
utterances.text: This was written by scriptor A. Scriptor A. And this was also entered by the same scriptor A, whereas this part of the content from the middle of the page down to the bottom of the page was written by scriptor C, obviously not the encircled part written by scriptor A.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Could you please mark the encircled parts with letters A and C, which would indicate to us exactly who the authors are. Thank you. You have told us that you also noticed some parts having been crossed out. Could you please point to the places where this happened and whether you can see the previous text under the crossing-out?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR GOGIC
utterances.text: This is in the penultimate line of the handwritten page. The crossing-out was carried out so that the previous content was not completely neutralised, which means that one can read the following words "PUK Beara", standing for Colonel Beara, underneath. By analyzing the ink, we determine that the same ink was used both for the original entry as well as for the crossed-out entry, so the same ballpoint pen was used.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Is there anything relevant that you would like to tell us about this particular page?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR GOGIC
utterances.text: I believe that I've told you everything.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. We will also tender this into evidence, but the procedure preceding that has to be the same. Please sign it, i.e., put your initials on the document and today's date. While Mr. Gogic is doing that, I would kindly ask for the following document, which is 02935744. The document is on the screen now. Kindly analyse this document based on your brief. Tell us exactly how many scriptors there were, one or several, and explain all the other things that you have established. And I will also kindly ask you to put the same type of markings on this document as well.

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR GOGIC
utterances.text: The handwritten content on the page bearing number 02935744 is a product of three different scriptors or writers. The first writer authored the content, and this scriptor I marked as scriptor A, from the top of the page to the word "Bajagica" and including that word. Writer B authored the contents of the last two paragraphs. Finally, Writer C -- I apologise, an unknown scriptor, entered the following entry, "14.07 Jokic." When I analysed the means of writing used, I determined that scriptor A used the same blue ballpoint pen. The first paragraph written by scriptor B was done by a different blue ballpoint pen, and for the second paragraph written by scriptor B, a different ballpoint pen was used. The content "14.07 Jokic" was entered with a graphite pencil. When it comes to the writing, this would be an example of sequential writing done by scriptors A and B. Here, we also have an example of a separate entry, i.e., an example of inserted content which, as I've already indicated, is in this case the entry "14.07 Jokic", which was entered separately between the last two paragraphs entered by scriptor B.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: What is the character of the entry "14.07 Jokic"? How would you describe this?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR GOGIC
utterances.text: As I've already told you, this is a separate inscription standing on its own which was entered by a different writer. This is best seen from a series of elements. For example, if you look at the way this person wrote the words and numbers in the structure, and we don't see that in Scriptor's B writing, and we see it in Scriptor's A writing, we will see that there is a separation between figures, that there's no slant, that numbers are vertical, that the numbers are extremely large, that there is a problem with the line of writing. These are all elements which undoubtedly point to a separate inscription. There's also another fact that cannot be ignored, although it is not always the most relevant, and the fact is that a different means of writing was used to make this entry.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: How could you determine that the entry "14.07 Jokic" was made with a different means of writing, and what means was that?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR GOGIC
utterances.text: I've already told you this was done by a graphite pencil, and this was determined when we analysed the ink that was carried out in the Dutch forensic institute here in The Hague. In that sense, I would kindly ask you to display from the CD.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry. We will have to ask you -- it will be much more efficient if you have those images that you took from the CD to put them on our display. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I am asking for this to be done because the material from the CD has still not been downloaded on e-court.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yeah, I have it in my briefcase, but I haven't got my briefcase on me here in the courtroom. It is in the room for the witnesses.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We have a technical problem. The witness has left the materials behind in the witness room. I don't know whether this would be a good moment to let the witness go since the Trial Chamber has asked for five minutes before the end of today's session. Maybe we could release the witness and continue with him -- his testimony tomorrow because I have other material to go through with him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: That's a good idea. Let the witness sign this document and keep it for the moment and continue tomorrow morning at 9.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I apologise. I would kindly ask the Trial Chamber to instruct the witness to have all of his materials on him tomorrow when he comes to the courtroom. This would certainly avoid any similar problems, any problems of the nature that we're facing at the moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. And Professor Gogic, you are advised not to contact any of the Defence team or Prosecutor to discuss the evidence you are going to give, so we'll meet again tomorrow morning, 9 o'clock.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And this is our ruling on the admission of statements we discussed about at the end of the testimony of Mr. Wagenaar. First of all, we would like to make sure that we are not dealing with this issue on a general basis. We are deciding whether or not to admit these documents with reference to this particular expert witness in the specific context of his report and evidence. In that context, we are of the view that documents contained in the binders should be admitted because they are important or helpful for a proper and full analysis of Professor Wagenaar's evidence. Therefore, we are admitting those statements but solely for that purpose and not for the truth of the contents. The same will apply to 2D603, Mr. Lutke's information report. However, as regards Mr. Malinic's interview, transcript, and summary, we will not admit them because we did not allow any question to be answered at the end of the day. That said, we'll adjourn for today, and we'll meet again at 9 o'clock tomorrow morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
